The STREAM Group aims to accelerate the development of current and future energy-related technologies by providing an atomistic-level understanding of key processes occurring at liquid–solid interfaces.

Our research focuses on aqueous and electrified interfaces. A central direction of the group is the study of electrochemical environments, where interfacial water, ions, applied potentials, and surface structure act together to determine reaction mechanisms and charge-transfer processes. We aim to understand these effects at the molecular level and to develop descriptors that can help guide the rational design of electrochemical interfaces. Two further threads run through this work: the quantum nature of the hydrogen nucleus, whose zero-point energy and tunnelling can shift reaction rates by orders of magnitude, and surface-specific vibrational spectroscopies, which provide the most direct bridge between our simulations and experiment.

To tackle these challenges, we develop and apply advanced first-principles simulation methods, complemented by machine-learning techniques that allow us to reach the accuracy and complexity required by the scientific question. We also develop path-integral methods to calculate quantum reaction rates, and theoretical approaches to simulate vibrational spectroscopies, including sum-frequency generation, tip-enhanced Raman, infrared, and Raman spectroscopy. Much of this work is contributed to open community codes such as i-PI and FHI-aims.

We enjoy collaborating with experimentalists and theoreticians alike to address challenging problems in interfacial chemistry, electrochemistry, spectroscopy, and energy-related materials.
